stem: A 54-year-old woman has had urinary infections again and again for 10 years. Urine pH is 8.0, with many white cells and coffin-lid shaped crystals. CT shows a large branching stone filling the left renal pelvis and calyces.
oneliner: 54F + 10 y of recurrent UTIs + urine pH 8.0 + coffin-lid crystals + branching stone filling the renal pelvis → which organism?
ask: Which organism most likely caused this stone?

whyNot.A: Commonest UTI cause, but **does not make urease**, so urine is not alkaline
whyNot.C: Catheters and hospital infections; **not a classic stone-former**
whyNot.E: **Sterile pyuria with acid urine**, calcified 'putty' kidney

why: **Alkaline urine + struvite (coffin-lid) crystals + staghorn calculus** = urease-splitting organism, classically **Proteus**.

bug.name: Proteus mirabilis
bug.lab: Swarming motility on agar; urease positive; makes H2S
bug.virulence: Urease; flagella for swarming up the urinary tract

stem: A 30-year-old man who injects drugs has had 5 days of fever and right-sided low back pain. He has no dysuria, frequency or flank trauma. Temperature is 38.9°C (102°F). Urinalysis is bland, and CT shows a fluid collection with a thick wall next to the right kidney. He has had no catheter or urologic procedure.
oneliner: 30M + injects drugs + 5 d fever and right low back pain + no urinary symptoms + bland urinalysis + abscess beside right kidney → organism?
ask: Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible?

whyNot.B: The usual cause when the abscess **follows an ascending urinary infection**; he has **no urinary symptoms and a bland urinalysis**
whyNot.C: Another ascending organism, linked to **stones and urinary infection**; neither is present
whyNot.D: Seen after **catheters or urologic procedures**; he has had none
whyNot.E: Ascending gram-negative infection after a **urinary infection**; he has none

why: **Injection drug use, fever, back pain, a perinephric abscess on CT, and a bland urinalysis with no urinary symptoms** = bloodborne seeding of the perirenal space, most often by **S. aureus**. An abscess that **ascends from pyelonephritis** is instead usually **gram-negative bacilli**.

bug.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bug.lab: Catalase positive, coagulase positive; golden colonies with beta-hemolysis; ferments mannitol
bug.virulence: Protein A binds the Fc of IgG, blocking opsonization; coagulase; toxins (TSST-1, exfoliatin, enterotoxin); PBP2a makes MRSA resistant
bug.spread: Skin and nasal flora; bloodborne seeding after skin injection; direct contact
bug.causes: Skin abscesses, endocarditis, osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, toxic shock, food poisoning, bloodborne perinephric abscess

idea.rule: The route decides the organism: bloodborne perinephric abscess is S. aureus, ascending is gram-negative bacilli.
also: Injection drug use: S. aureus causes right-sided (tricuspid) endocarditis
Hematogenous vertebral osteomyelitis is usually S. aureus
Proteus mirabilis makes struvite stones after ascending infection
E. coli is the most common cause of pyelonephritis and of ascending perinephric abscess
